headline: Gmail arrived on April Fools' Day, TheFacebook opened to students, and the year ended with the tsunami
texture: Google put out Gmail on April 1 and people assumed the gigabyte of storage was a joke. TheFacebook launched from a Harvard dorm room and stayed inside universities. Broadband passed dial-up as the way most Americans online got there, and half the country still heard a modem when it connected. Shrek 2 took $929 million worldwide, the year's biggest. The Passion of the Christ came fifth with $611 million, playing partly in Aramaic.

Al-Qaeda bombed four commuter trains in Madrid on March 11, killing at least 192 people. Photographs from Abu Ghraib came out in April and showed American soldiers torturing Iraqi prisoners. Chechen fighters took over a school in Beslan on September 1 with 1,128 hostages, most of them children. Bush was reelected on November 2. Ukraine's Orange Revolution started on November 22 over an election nobody believed.

The European Union took in ten new members on May 1, most of them east of the old line. The Athens Olympics ran from August 13 to 29. The Boston Red Sox won the World Series and ended eighty-six years without one. On December 26 an earthquake off Sumatra measured between 9.1 and 9.3 and the tsunami it sent out killed people on coastlines thousands of miles apart.

notes: Research pass July 2026. Box office is worldwide gross, which is what the source ranks. The broadband fact reuses the Pew report cited in tech_firsts, and states its denominator, because half of home internet users is a different claim from half of households. Facebook carries no date field: the year article gives no launch date and a date invented to fill the field would be exactly the kind of error this project is trying not to make.
